title: Bearings and Loci
seo_title: Year 9 Bearings and Loci Worksheets: Three-Figure Bearings, Back Bearings and Constructions
standard_text: Use the standard conventions for labelling and referring to the sides and angles of triangles; draw diagrams from written description; use standard ruler and compass constructions (perpendicular bisector, angle bisector) and understand loci; interpret bearings.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 bearings and loci worksheets: read three-figure bearings, back bearings, compass directions, loci (circles, perpendicular and angle bisectors) and map problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Bearings: clockwise from north, three figures.
body_html:
How it works

A bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north, written with three figures: 045°, 120°, 300°. The bearing of B from A is measured at A. The back bearing (A from B) is 180° more or less.

A locus is the set of points that follow a rule. Fixed distance from a point: a circle. Equidistant from two points: the perpendicular bisector. Equidistant from two lines: the angle bisector.

Example

The bearing of B from A is 065°. Find the bearing of A from B.

065° + 180°.

Answer: 245°

Example

The anticlockwise angle from north to AB is 110°.

360° − 110°.

Answer: 250°

Example

Where are points 4 cm from P?

Same distance from one point.

Answer: A circle, radius 4 cm

Common mistakes

  • Measuring anticlockwise or from the wrong point.
  • Writing 45° instead of 045°.
  • Getting a back bearing over 360°. If the bearing is more than 180°, subtract 180°.
  • Using the perpendicular bisector when the rule is about two lines (use the angle bisector).

faq.a: An angle measured clockwise from north, written with three figures, such as 045° or 230°.

faq.q: How do I find a back bearing?
faq.a: Add 180° if the bearing is less than 180°; subtract 180° if it is more.
The set of all points that follow a rule, such as 'exactly 3 cm from P', which is a circle.

faq.q: When do I use a perpendicular bisector or an angle bisector?
faq.a: Perpendicular bisector: equidistant from two points. Angle bisector: equidistant from two lines.

items.q: A walker faces north and turns clockwise to face north-east. How many degrees does she turn?
items.e: North is 000° and north-east is 045°. Clockwise: 45°.

items.q: A walker faces north-east and turns clockwise to face west. How many degrees does she turn?
items.e: North-east is 045° and west is 270°. Clockwise: 225°.

items.q: What is the three-figure bearing for the direction south-west?
items.e: Measure clockwise from north. South-west is 225°.

items.q: What is the three-figure bearing for the direction north-east?
items.e: Measure clockwise from north. North-east is 045°.

items.q: A plane flies on a bearing of 165°. In which direction is it flying?
c: It is between south and west
It is between east and south
It is between west and north
It is between north and east
items.e: 165° is between 090° and 180°, so it is between east and south.

items.q: What is the three-figure bearing for the direction north-west?
items.e: Measure clockwise from north. North-west is 315°.

items.q: What is the three-figure bearing for the direction west?
items.e: Measure clockwise from north. West is 270°.

items.q: What is the three-figure bearing for the direction north?
items.e: Measure clockwise from north. North is 000°.

items.q: A plane flies on a bearing of 345°. In which direction is it flying?
c: It is between west and north
It is between east and south
It is between north and east
It is between south and west
items.e: 345° is between 270° and 360°, so it is between west and north.

items.q: A walker faces south and turns clockwise to face south-west. How many degrees does she turn?
items.e: South is 180° and south-west is 225°. Clockwise: 45°.

items.q: A plane flies on a bearing of 080°. In which direction is it flying?

It is between west and north
It is between east and south
It is between south and west
items.e: 080° is between 000° and 090°, so it is between north and east.

items.q: A walker faces north-east and turns clockwise to face south-east. How many degrees does she turn?

items.q: The locus of points exactly 3 cm from a point P is…
c: A circle with centre P and radius 3 cm
items.e: Every point 3 cm from P lies on a circle with centre P and radius 3 cm.

items.q: The locus of points less than 3 cm from a point P is…
c: The region inside a circle of radius 3 cm, centre P
A circle of radius 3 cm only
The region outside a circle of radius 3 cm
items.e: Less than 3 cm means inside the circle: the region inside a circle of radius 3 cm, centre P.

items.q: The locus of points equidistant from two points A and B is…
c: A circle through A and B
items.e: Points the same distance from A and B lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB.

items.q: The locus of points equidistant from two lines that meet at a point is…
c: A line parallel to one of the lines
items.e: Points the same distance from two crossing lines lie on the angle bisector.

items.q: The locus of points exactly 2 cm from a straight line (going on forever) is…
c: Two parallel lines, 2 cm either side
items.e: On each side of the line there is a parallel line 2 cm away: two parallel lines, 2 cm either side.

items.q: The locus of points exactly 2 cm from a line segment AB is…
c: Two parallel lines joined by semicircles at A and B
items.e: Beside the segment the points form parallel lines; around each end they form semicircles. The shape is like a running track.

items.q: A goat is tied to a post with a 5 m rope. Which shape shows where it can graze?
c: A circle of radius 5 m, including the inside
items.e: It can reach any point up to 5 m from the post: a circle of radius 5 m, including the inside.

items.q: A goat is tied to a 4 m rope that can slide along a 10 m rail. Which shape shows where it can graze?
c: A 10 m by 4 m rectangle only
A rectangle with a semicircle at each end
items.e: Points within 4 m of a segment: a rectangle with a semicircle at each end.

items.q: Which construction gives points the same distance from towns A and B?
c: A line through B parallel to AB
items.e: Equidistant from two points means the perpendicular bisector of AB.

items.q: Which construction gives points the same distance from two walls of a room that meet at a corner?
c: The angle bisector of the corner
A circle centred on the corner
A line parallel to one wall
The perpendicular bisector of the walls
items.e: Equidistant from two lines means the angle bisector of the corner.

items.q: Points closer to A than to B lie…
c: On B's side of the perpendicular bisector of AB
On A's side of the perpendicular bisector of AB
items.e: The perpendicular bisector divides the plane. Points closer to A are on A's side of the perpendicular bisector.

items.q: A phone mast reaches 20 km. Which shape shows the area it covers?
c: A circle of radius 20 km, including the inside
items.e: Every point within 20 km: a circle of radius 20 km, including the inside.

items.q: To draw a perpendicular bisector of AB with compasses, the compass width must be…
items.e: The arcs from A and B must cross, so the width must be more than half of AB.

items.q: Which is equidistant from both sides of angle ABC?
c: A point on the line AC
A point on the perpendicular bisector of AB
A point on the bisector of angle ABC
items.e: Points on the angle bisector are the same distance from BA and BC: a point on the bisector of angle ABC.

items.q: Treasure is buried 3 m from tree T and the same distance from posts P and Q. Where should you dig?
c: On the angle bisector at T
Where the circle round T meets the perpendicular bisector of PQ
items.e: Use both loci: the circle of radius 3 m round T and the perpendicular bisector of PQ. Dig where they meet.

items.q: The locus of points exactly 5 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm is…
items.e: Every point of the circle is 5 cm from its centre, so the locus is the circle itself.

items.q: Points more than 2 m from a wall and less than 6 m from a lamp are shown by…
items.e: Each condition gives a region. The answer is the overlap of two regions.

items.q: Which tools do you need to construct an angle bisector?
items.e: Constructions use compasses and a ruler, not a protractor.

items.q: The locus of the tip of a clock's hour hand over 12 hours is…
items.e: The tip stays the same distance from the centre: a circle.

items.q: Points equidistant from the lines y = 2 and y = 8 lie on…
items.e: Halfway between two parallel lines: (2 + 8) ÷ 2 = 5, so the line y = 5.

items.q: A ship sails 5 km on a bearing of 090°, then 5 km on a bearing of 180°. What is its bearing from the start?
items.e: It has gone 5 km east and 5 km south, so it is south-east of the start: 135°.

items.q: From the start, the ship is south-east. What is the bearing of the start from the ship?
On a map, 1 cm represents 2 km. A boat is 7.5 cm from a port. How far is that in real life?
A scale is 1 : 50,000. Two villages are 6 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they?
The bearing of B from A is 070°. The bearing of C from A is 160°. What is angle BAC?
Which of these is not a correctly written bearing?
items.e: Bearings have three figures, so 45° should be written 045°. 45° is not correct.

items.q: A hiker walks on a bearing of 200°. Which direction is closest?
items.e: 200° is just past south (180°), towards west: south-south-west.

items.q: A plane flies due west and then turns to fly due north. Through how many degrees has it turned clockwise?
items.e: West is 270° and north is 360°: it turns 90° clockwise.

items.q: The bearing of X from Y is 310°. What is the bearing of Y from X?
items.e: 310° − 180° = 130°. Subtract 180° when the bearing is more than 180°.

items.q: A lighthouse L is due north of a port P. A ship S is due east of L. What is the bearing of S from P?
items.e: S is north and east of P, so the bearing is between 000° and 090°.

items.q: A boat is 8 km from a port on a bearing of 090°. A buoy is 6 km from the port on a bearing of 000°. How far is the boat from the buoy?
items.e: The bearings are 90° apart, so use Pythagoras: √(8² + 6²) = 10 km.

items.q: A sprinkler waters up to 3 m away. It is placed in the middle of a 4 m by 4 m lawn. Does it water the whole lawn?
c: No, the edges are 3 m away
No, the corners are 4 m away
Yes, the corners are less than 3 m away
items.e: The corners are √(2² + 2²) ≈ 2.83 m from the middle. Yes, the corners are less than 3 m away.

items.q: A dog is tied to the corner of a shed (outside) with a 3 m rope. The shed walls meet at 90°. What fraction of a circle can it reach?
items.e: The shed blocks a 90° corner, so it reaches 270° of the circle: ¾.

items.q: What is the bearing of south-west?
items.e: South-west is halfway between south (180°) and west (270°): 225°.

items.q: Two ships leave port. One sails on 040°, the other on 130°. What is the angle between their paths?
Ava measures the bearing of B from A anticlockwise and gets 60°. What is the correct bearing?
items.e: Bearings are measured clockwise: 360° − 60° = 300°.

items.q: A ship is 12 km due south of a port. What is the bearing of the port from the ship?
items.e: The port is due north of the ship: 000°.

items.q: Where do the perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle meet?
c: At the midpoint of the longest side
At a point the same distance from all three corners
items.e: Each bisector is equidistant from two corners, so where they meet is the same distance from all three corners.

items.q: A radio mast covers 30 km. Town T is 25 km away on a bearing of 050°. Can people in T hear it?
c: No, 25 km is outside the range
items.e: The range is a circle of radius 30 km in every direction. Yes, 25 km is within 30 km.

items.q: On a 1 : 25,000 map, how many centimetres show 1 km?
